notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.13

Faster test runs
• Work Item VMs are now sized from your Mac: most of its cores and a safe share of its memory when one run is active, shared fairly when several are. On a 16 GB Mac a single run gets about 8 GB instead of 4.
• Your project's tests use every core the VM has, within memory.
• The build no longer waits for your whole test suite to run first. When the same commit was measured before, that result is reused; otherwise Vekrun checks that the tests start, the build begins, and the full baseline runs later beside the proof. The proof still runs your whole suite.
• The throwaway test PostgreSQL, Redis and Elasticsearch in the VM run with test-friendly settings.
• The proof VM is prepared while the agent works on 16 GB Macs too.

Resume continues exactly
• "Continue" picks up the same Work Item from the step where it stopped, reusing its VM, setup, commits, plan and baseline when they still fit, and says what it reused.
• Updating Vekrun while a run is active now offers "Update when the run finishes" or "Pause the run and update", instead of stopping the run.
• A prepared VM that was stopped while Vekrun was closed is started again, or rebuilt, by Vekrun itself. You are never asked to run a terminal command.
• A stopped run shows one card, naming the step it really stopped at, with its error in plain words.

Rails projects
• Vekrun loads your Rails test key (config/credentials/test.key) and local .env files from your project folder automatically, after checking they are for testing. Production and master keys, and values that look like live keys, are never loaded. You are asked to paste a key only when the file is missing. A per-project switch in Environment turns this off.
• Test failures caused only by a missing Rails test key are reported as that, not as your project's failing tests.
• Tailwind setup no longer runs generators or changes tracked files while preparing the environment.

Spending you can trust
• A model call that never reached the provider costs $0. Earlier builds could count a refused call at its reservation (one Work Item showed $3.69 for $0.19 of real spend); those old rows are corrected on update.
• When a call ends without a price, Vekrun asks OpenRouter what it actually cost and records that.
• New OpenRouter models are priced from OpenRouter's own list, so they run under a spending cap.
• The budget card shows confirmed spend apart from amounts held for calls still awaiting their price.

Seeing what's happening
• Live progress from the Coordinator, the Council and the checks (check writer, judge, reviewer), with heartbeats, the model each one uses, and its own label.
• AI Factory: running Work Items are pinned to the top with an "In progress" badge, their stage and a running clock. Items that need you say so. A run that is no longer running says that.
• The Plan card reads "Plan · Coordinator" when no Council met, shows the verdict and the reasoning clearly, renders code, and uses the full width. The status pill no longer says "Council deliberating" when no Council met.
